text: I’ve been using Spark for many years across many devices (iPhone, multiple iPads, multiple MacBooks, Mac mini, pc) and it is the most clean and well functioning client. I’ve used both the free and paid tiers and am currently back on free tier which is perfect for a regular person. All your mail is stored on sparks servers and syncs perfectly across devices. The layout is clean and the ui is functional. I prefer the simple inbox and that’s true no matter which client I’m using. I just find it much easier to search and organize instead of grouping emails, but that’s probably just because I’m old school and used to it this way. If you’re a Gmail user you might know that you can’t use apple stock mail client without huge frustration. Every time I plug my phone in the charger I get bombarded with days of email notifications rapidly firing on my watch and phone. It’s the most annoying frustrating thing ever to happen every single time you charge your phone. It’s not apple’s fault; google blocks users from using push on apple mail app so you’re forced to use fetch. No matter what frequency you choose to fetch it still causes Gmail to fetch every time you plug in and since I have two Gmail accounts it’s a lot of notifications. I get email notifications for mail I already checked! It’s Google’s push to get users to use the Gmail app but I don’t like it as much as spark. Spark doesn’t have the issue apple does so I can use my favorite client without getting 50 notifications machine gunning my phone and watch every time power is connected. This app is great and the only one I’ll ever need for my purposes. Give it a try.

I’ve tried SuperHuman and it was phenomenal but for someone that uses it just for personal use I could not afford that price every month then I came across Spark+AI and WOW it is amazing. The app UI is clean and amazing in appearance. The free trial was amazing and I’m still trying to figure out to get it set up just to my likings and my free trial ran out and honestly didn’t even realize the trial was over right away, that’s how many amazing features Spark gives you. $7.99/month is a lot more affordable than the alternatives I’ve come across but do wish they offered a student price. For someone like me with ADHD, this is very helpful to keep my emails sorted, organized and inboxes cleaned out. Before they were absolute chaos. The only major improvements that would be great is if the calendar UI/appearance looked as good as the rest of the application. Also if they could work with other applications like Structured (one I use to stay on top of my days and plan them out because of my ADHD, it helps me stay focused on things I need to get done), some sort of integration where I could either import events from there into Spark or vice versa. Overall, I will say that Spark+AI helps me stay on top of my emails, important emails personal, work/business and university without feeling overwhelmed and bombarded. Keep up the great work and I look forward to the future of Spark!!

I love this app... however, the basic features of an email app have not been focused on. As an app developer, I understand what it takes to do this and is not lost on me at all. There are a few key things that need to be addressed before the Spark team releases new features or paid plans. 1. Fix the search feature. Unless your search term is exactly what you need, the search won't return anything (including a message saying no results found). On the desktop side, trying to drag the cursor in the search field actually drags the entire app. Extremely frustrating. 2. Fix the notification issue. Notification badges stopped working for me and I have no way of fixing. The settings inside the app allow you to turn on the badges and notifications, but once I do, I get a message saying it's unsupported. 3. Add spam learning or filters. This is the most I've ever had to deal with spam mitigation. This shouldn't be a paid feature either. Again, the app is great and has so much potential but I'm willing to remove my account if it means a more efficient experience with email. Hoping the team takes this as constructive. Based on previous reviews that have ripped the app, I'm sure I'll get a basic response to email the dev support team. I've already done that (multiple times). Please spare me the patronizing response you have given others and just take action on what people are suggesting.

I really, and I mean REALLY want to love this app. On the surface it’s everything you could want in an email client. Lately however, problems have crept in making it annoying to use, particularly between devices, where if I delete or arrange messages into relevant folders, it’s all cleaned up on one device, but when i switch to say… my phone… all the messages are still there in the inbox. It isn’t until I kill the app and do a pulldown refresh that the state of the inbox is actually refreshed. On top of that, on any given device at any given time, I’ll check my mail, clean out my inbox and flick the app away, only to discover the red dot with my message count hasn’t updated and it looks like I still have unread messages. To be fair this could just be an issue in ios, but I don’t have this issue with other apps so I dunno. Today, and what prompted me to finally leave a cautionary review - I actually had to delete and reinstall spark on my ipad to get it to realize i had already read and filed my messages on my phone.Minor annoyances to be sure, but as Readdle continues on their corporate path of “we can always make it better” - you’re breaking too much. Change is bad, ok. we spend years building email habits and expectations, and believe me, rocking a comfortable boat with more going on under the hood than you can keep working reliably is not the way. NOT THE WAY.

As many have stated, I was also a mailbox user and I was very disappointed at the Dropbox decision to drop the best mail app created. I was pleasantly surprised to see this app, but the biggest flaw I have noticed so far is that it cannot open a password protected excel doc. I like the swipes, the signatures, the snooze, the price, the look and feel, most things, but as others have mentioned there are some flaws that need to be addressed. Over the native app it has the snooze which is crucial to me. Please keep making improvements, I've looked though some of the future development and it looks like it is going to be very good, but don't forget about basic email functionality. EDIT: After using spark for awhile now I do like it but it has some really annoying features. For instance, when I download the images of a Google news alert, spark only renders the visible screen and you cannot scroll around to see the rest of the message. I see this with many html messages. This should work as a going in argument when releasing an email app in today's world. EDIT 2: They have fixed the html annoyances, the html rendering is flawless and smooth, it now rotates to landscape & portrait. I LOVE this app. Probably the best mail reader out there, it has surpassed mailbox by far!

UPDATE: Spark has since patched this app, so the bottom complaint is no longer relevant but the effect of it still sours things slightly, so I don’t know that I can give this 5 stars. This app is a good app again though. —————-(The following a copy of an email I sent to support. This was a 5 star app now reduced to a 1 star app that I will be forced to stop using due to this problem.)I’ve been using Spark for almost 3 years now. I use it professionally. I am upset that I am forced to have a “Sent with Spark“ signature at the end of any email I send out. The only way I can disable this is to pay you a significant amount of money a year. I have looked at what your premium service offers and unfortunately you are offering nothing extra with premium that I need or desire. Basically, you are asking me to spend $42 in order to get rid of an annoyance signature tag. Please consider allowing free users to disable “Sent with Spark” in your very next update or grandfathering previous purchasers of your product into not having to deal with this built-in annoyance meant to compel us into upgrading our service. I am happy to see that your business is growing, but it should not be done this way. Alternatively, I would be happy to purchase a “disable Sent with Spark“ add-on purchase for a reasonable amount such as five dollars, though that probably wouldn’t please everyone of your long-time user-base, but I understand.

I have no complaints, but after a handful of experiences where while typing up a lengthy email draft, all of my text spontaneously disappears as if Ive typed nothing, Im here to request a serious UNDO button.

Mailbox.org (Dovecot) enforces a limit on simultaneous IMAP authentication events. With K-9/Thunderbird for Android, having multiple folders configured for push opens one IDLE connection per folder (via `ImapBackendPusher`'s folder → pusher map). Each connection authenticates independently and re-authenticates every 15 minutes on IDLE refresh. On accounts where other clients also connect frequently, the combined auth event rate can trigger Dovecot's rate limit, resulting in a persistent "Authentication Limit Exceeded" block that locks out all clients.

Compared with the Windows version of Thunderbird, the Android client currently offers a rather limited feature set and lacks meaningful customization. For instance, email translation cannot be performed within the app, and message encryption requires installing a separate third-party application. [...] In addition, I would hope that the mobile client could achieve true real-time message delivery (push) when synchronizing mail across accounts, rather than relying on polling, so that new messages arrive more promptly and conveniently.
